title: Valid Palindrome
statement:
Decide whether a piece of text reads the same forward and backward.

Contract
- `text` is non-null and may be empty. It contains only printable ASCII
  characters (codes 32 through 126).
- Only letters and digits count. Skip spaces, punctuation, and every other
  character.
- Compare letters without regard to case, so `A` matches `a`. A digit only
  matches the same digit.
- Return true exactly when the letters and digits read the same in both
  directions. Text with no letters or digits reads the same both ways.

Examples
- `isPalindrome("Was it a car or a cat I saw?")` returns `true`.
- `isPalindrome("race a car")` returns `false`.
- `isPalindrome(".,!")` returns `true`.

examples.input: text = "Was it a car or a cat I saw?"

hints: Building a cleaned, lowercased copy and comparing it with its reverse works, but it allocates two extra strings.
Walk one index in from each end, and skip any character that is neither a letter nor a digit before comparing.
Compare Character.toLowerCase of the two characters, move both indexes inward on a match, and stop when they meet. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: the text between single quotes, for example: 'Was it a car or a cat I saw?'
sampleInput: 'Was it a car or a cat I saw?'
